title: How do equal groups with some left over become expressions?
description: Thirty three students make equal groups of different sizes, with one student sitting out, and each grouping is written as an expression and split into terms. Keeko's doubt is that the number the teacher calls is the number of groups.
teaching_notes: One idea: the number called is the size of each group, so the groups times that size, plus the students left over, give the thirty three. Ask the child to check each expression by working out its terms.

source: {{NAME_4}} sat out of a game and the other 33 students made equal
video_script.why: The child sees equal groups with a leftover written as a times term plus a single term, three times over.
video_script.substitution: Change the number of students and the size of the group and the method stays the same: groups times size, plus those left over.
video_script.anchor: thirty three students standing in equal groups, with a few left over
video_script.wrong_answer: the number called is the number of groups
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the number the teacher calls as the number of groups, when it is the size of each group.
video_script.payoff_line: Each expression has the value thirty three.

final_answer.spoken: six times five plus three, eight times four plus one, and four times seven plus five, each with value thirty three

names.{{NAME_4}}: everyday child, not a character of the book

maths_rules: called 5: 33 = 6 groups of 5 with 3 left, so 6 x 5 + 3 = 30 + 3 = 33; terms 6 x 5 and 3
called 4: 33 = 8 groups of 4 with 1 left, so 8 x 4 + 1 = 32 + 1 = 33; terms 8 x 4 and 1
called 7: 33 = 4 groups of 7 with 5 left, so 4 x 7 + 5 = 28 + 5 = 33; terms 4 x 7 and 5
the slip: 5 groups would be 5 x 6 + 3 = 33 only if each group had 6, not 5
video_script.design: One idea: groups times size, plus those left over. The students in groups stay in the anchor band; the working band writes each expression and its terms. Keeko's doubt: the number called is the number of groups.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>{{NAME_4}} sits out of a game.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The other thirty three students make equal groups.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The teacher calls five, and groups of five form.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>{{NAME_4}} writes six times five plus three.
What will the expressions be if the teacher calls four, or seven?

<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three students are left over.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The call is the size of each group, and the groups are counted.

beats.on_screen: Given: 33 students in equal groups; the leftover students are in one group of their own; called 5 gives 6 × 5 + 3
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, thirty three students make equal groups, and the extra students are left over.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>For five, the expression is six times five plus three.

beats.on_screen: To find: the expression when 4 is called; the expression when 7 is called; the terms of each

marks.m2: the words terms of each are added

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to write the expression when four is called, and when seven is called.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We also list the terms of each, which are the parts separated by the plus sign.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: called 5: 33 = 6 groups of 5 and 3 left; 6 × 5 + 3; terms 6 × 5 and 3

marks.m1: 6 groups of 5 and 3 left is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, when five is called, we get six groups of five, with three left.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That is six times five plus three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The terms are six times five, and three.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: called 4: 33 = 8 groups of 4 and 1 left; 8 × 4 + 1; terms 8 × 4 and 1

marks.m1: 8 groups of 4 and 1 left is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, when four is called, we get eight groups of four, with one left.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That is eight times four plus one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The terms are eight times four, and one.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: called 7: 33 = 4 groups of 7 and 5 left; 4 × 7 + 5; terms 4 × 7 and 5

marks.m1: 4 groups of 7 and 5 left is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, when seven is called, we get four groups of seven, with five left.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That is four times seven plus five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The terms are four times seven, and five.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check by working out each term first.
Thirty plus three is thirty three, as it should be.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirty two plus one is thirty three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Twenty eight plus five is thirty three.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Calling five gives us six times five plus three.
Calling four gives eight times four plus one.
Calling seven gives four times seven plus five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Each expression has the value thirty three.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the number called is the number of groups.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But when the teacher called five, there were six groups.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The call is the size of each group.
